la:adj:pravus.html:
prāvus, a, um, adj.
cf. Sanscr. prahva, crooked
,
crooked, not straight, distorted, misshapen, deformed (opp. rectus; class.).
Lit.: prava, cubantia, prona, supina atque absona tecta,: si quae in membris prava, aut debilitata aut imminuta sunt,: talus,.—Absol.: in pravum, into crookedness (post-Aug.): elapsi in pravum artus,: quae in pravum induruerunt,.—
Trop., perverse, irregular, improper, wrong, vicious, bad (syn.: improbus, malus, nequam).
Of living beings: pravus factus est,: impulsores,: pravissimus homo,: quae belua ruptis, Cum semel effugit, reddit se prava catenis? i. e. stulta, incauta,.—
With gen. (poet.): pravus fidei,faithless,: pravus togae,: audendi pravus,.—
Of things: nihil pravum, perversum,: affectio,: dociles imitandis Turpibus et pravis omnes sumus,: a rectis in vitia, a vitiis in prava, a pravis in praecipitia pervenitur,: ad honesta, seu prava juxta levis,: aemulatio,: spes,.—Comp.: quo pravius nihil esse possit, .—Sup.: pravissima consuetudinis regula,.—Absol.: in pravum, in perversity: frangas citius, quam corrigas, quae in pravum induruerunt,.—Hence, adv.: prāvē, crookedly; trop., improperly, wrongly, amiss, ill, badly (opp. recte; class.): hoc mihi videtur factum prave,: prave (facta), opp. recte facta,: ille porro male, prave, nequiter, turpiter cenabat,: prave sectus unguis,: sive ego prave, Seu recte hoc volui,: prave facti versus,: pudens prave,: prave aliquid intellegere,: prave detorta verba,: facundus,: prave et perperam appellare,.—Sup.: pravissume, Sall. Or. Lepidi adv. Sull.

la:noun:pravitas.html:
prāvĭtas, ātis, f.
pravus
,
crookedness, inequality, irregularity, deformity (class.).
Lit.: pravitas membrorum,: corporis pravitates,: oris,a distorting of the mouth in speaking,; : statuminum,: curvaturae,.—
Trop., irregularity, impropriety, bad condition, perverseness: quae ista est pravitas Quaeve amentia?: ne malā consuetudine ad aliquam deformitatem pravitatemque veniamus, impropriety in speaking, in gestures, etc., : ominis,a bad omen,: tortuosae orationis,.—
In partic., of character, viciousness, untowardness, perverseness, depravity: animi,perverseness,: mentis,: in istā pravitate perstabitis?: consilii,: interitus pravitatis,; : morum,: cordis, et saep.
